title: 辩论：越想要越得不到的东西，该怎么要？
title_en: How do you pursue what pursuit drives away?

questions.question: 对睡眠、灵感这类越用力越远的东西，按这场辩论的共识，最可取的做法是什么？
options: 完全不用力，什么都不安排，静静等它自己到来
把它当成纯技能，每天按固定时长反复刻意练习
对结果加倍用力，持续监测进展以便随时调整
对动作和条件用力，同时撤掉对结果的实时查岗
questions.explanation: 共识是：能直接做的是动作和条件，不能直接做的是对结果的检查。比如睡眠的动作是固定起床、睡不着就离床，分数是手环和「睡着没」，只做动作那一栏、把分数那一栏关掉。什么都不安排同样被否定，修路、作息都是要主动去做的。
questions.question_en: For things like sleep and inspiration that recede the harder you chase them, what does this debate's consensus recommend?
options_en: Make no effort at all, arrange nothing, and wait for it to come on its own
Treat it purely as a skill and drill it deliberately for a fixed time daily
Push harder on the result itself, monitoring progress closely to adjust
Put effort into actions and conditions, while dropping real-time checks on the result
questions.explanation_en: The consensus: actions and conditions can be done directly; checking the result can't. For sleep, the actions are a fixed wake time and leaving bed when awake, the score is the tracker and 'am I asleep yet'; do the actions and switch off the score. Arranging nothing was rejected too: building the path and keeping a schedule take active effort.

questions.question: 一个失眠的人每晚盯着手环的睡眠分数，越盯越睡不着。按辩论中给出的机制，问题出在哪里？
options: 用力时后台有个查岗的监控者，人一累，它要找的失败信号就占满了脑子
过度关注睡眠会让人白天减少活动，夜里身体不够疲劳
手环屏幕的蓝光会抑制褪黑素分泌，从生理上直接干扰入睡
睡眠分数往往并不准确，错误的数据让人对自己的作息做出了错误调整
questions.explanation: 这是讽刺性加工的解释：控制心灵时，执行者去够你要的状态，监控者在后台查你失败没有。人一累，执行者没力气了，查岗的照常上班，它找的失败信号就占满脑子。所以用力本身不坏，坏在多了一个查岗的。
questions.question_en: An insomniac checks their sleep-tracker score every night and sleeps worse the more they watch it. Using the mechanism offered in the debate, what's going wrong?
options_en: Effort brings a background monitor checking for failure, and when you're tired its failure signal fills your mind
Focusing on sleep makes people less active by day, so they aren't tired enough at night
Blue light from the tracker suppresses melatonin and physically disrupts sleep
Sleep scores are often inaccurate, so bad data leads to wrong adjustments
questions.explanation_en: This is ironic process theory: when you control your mind, an operator reaches for the desired state while a monitor checks for failure. When you're tired the operator weakens but the monitor keeps working, and the failure it's scanning for floods your mind. Effort isn't the problem; the extra checker is.

questions.question: 被爱、被信任这类副产品，和睡眠、灵感相比，有什么关键不同？
options: 它还要另一个人同意，你再怎么不查岗，对方也有完全的自由不给
它比睡眠更依赖生理条件，必须先把作息和身体状态调整好
它完全不受自己行为的影响，努力与否最后的结果都是一样的
它可以直接通过请求得到，只要把自己的需要讲清楚，就一定能拿得到
questions.explanation: 总结补充的维度：睡眠、灵感只跟自己的心有关，绕开查岗就够了；被爱还要另一个人同意，你可以把需要说具体、提出请求，但要允许对方拒绝。所以对这一类，要放下的还有「我做对了就该得到」那本账。
questions.question_en: How do by-products like being loved or trusted differ crucially from sleep or inspiration?
options_en: They also need another person's consent; however little you monitor, the other person is free to withhold them
They depend even more on physiology, so you must fix your sleep and health first
They are entirely unaffected by your own behavior; effort makes no difference
They can be had just by asking; state your needs clearly and you'll get them
questions.explanation_en: The summary adds this dimension: sleep and inspiration involve only your own mind, so getting rid of the checker is enough. Being loved needs someone else's consent; you can make specific requests, but must allow a no. For these, you also have to drop the ledger that says 'if I do it right, I'm owed it.'
